summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) expand the residual stream of a Transformer into N parallel streams, and manifold-constrained HC (mHC) stabilizes them at scale. However, mHC benefits little from more than four streams, partly because each sublayer writes a single output to all streams, limiting how differently they can be updated.
takeaways: On a 1.1B model trained on 100B tokens, TPHC reduces validation loss by 0.7-1.0% and raises average zero-shot accuracy across six commonsense reasoning benchmarks by 0.3-0.7 percentage points relative to mHC at matched stream counts Nin{4,8,16}.
This design makes the residual-stream updates more expressive without adding parameters or FLOPs to the attention or FFN sublayers.
With native support for stream sharding under TP, TPHC requires only 9% more training time than mHC on an 8B model when both use four streams.
